题目为2026年10月21日记录的口语试题，注意时效性

Part 1

Friends

Questions:

  • Do you have a friend you have known for a long time?

    Yes. My closest friend is someone I met on my first day of primary school.

    We’ve maintained our friendship for over two decades, navigating different schools, universities, and cities. That long shared history has created an unbreakable bond and a deep intuitive understanding of each other.

  • Do you often go out with your friends?

    I would say we have a good balance. We make a point to schedule proper outings like trying a new restaurant or going to an exhibition a couple of times a month.

    But we also value simpler, more frequent interactions, like a quick coffee or a phone call, which are just as important for maintaining our connection.

  • Do you prefer to spend time with one friend or with a group of friends?

    I appreciate both dynamics for different reasons.

    One on one time allows for deeper, more intimate and vulnerable conversations.

    Group settings, however, are fantastic for energy, laughter and shared experiences. I don’t have a strong preference.

    It depends entirely on my mood and what I’m seeking from the social interaction.

  • How important are friends to you?

    They are utterly vital. My friends are my chosen family.

    They provide a crucial support system, emotional sustenance, and shared joy. They offer different perspectives, honest advice, and unconditional support through life’s challenges. Making the good times better and the hard times easier to bear.

  • Is there a difference between where you meet friends now and where you used to meet them in the past?

    There’s a significant difference in our teens and early 20s. We almost exclusively met in public places like shopping malls, cinemas, or fast food restaurants.

    Now, as adults, we gravitate much more towards each other’s homes for dinner, or quieter cafes and pubs where we can actually hear each other talk.

  • What do you usually do with your friends?

    Our activities are quite varied. We often go out for meals or coffee to catch up, go for walks in the park or watch films together. Sometimes our meet UPS are even more low key. Just spending an evening, cooking dinner together and talking at home is just as enjoyable.

  • Where do you often meet each other?

    We tend to favor casual, comfortable environments where we can talk without shouting.

    Our most common meeting spots are cozy cafes, each other’s homes or parks when the weather is nice.

    The location is always chosen for its ability to facilitate good conversation.

  • Why are some places suitable for meeting while others are not?

    Suitability hinges on the desired interaction. A noisy sports bar is perfect for watching a match with a group, but terrible for a heart to heart conversation. A library is suitable for studying together, but not for a celebratory party.

    The ideal venue matches the group size and the primary goal of the meeting be it lively socializing or intimate talking.

  • Would you invite friends to your home?

    Absolutely. I consider it the highest form of hospitality and intimacy.

    Inviting someone into your personal space is a sign of trust and comfort.

    Some of my best memories with friends are of informal gatherings at home, cooking together, playing games, and talking for hours without the time constraints of a public venue.

Advertisement

Questions:

  • Do you like advertisements?

    I appreciate well crafted creative advertisements that tell a story or artistically executed. However, I have a strong aversion to intrusive, repetitive, or blatantly manipulative ads. The sheer volume of advertising we are exposed to daily is overwhelming.

    So the ones that earn my attention are those that offer something of value, be it, humour, beauty, or useful Information.

  • Do you often see advertisements when you are on your phone or computer?

    Yes. I frequently encounter advertisements while using my phone or computer. In fact, digital ads are almost unavoidable in China, appearing on social media platforms within apps and as pre roll videos.

    While some can be intrusive, I find many useful, especially those tailored to my interests.

    As they often introduce me to new products or services, I might genuinely like.

  • Do you see a lot of advertising on trains or other transport？

    An enormous amount. Public transport is a prime advertising, real estate, because it captures a captive audience with little else to do during their commute, the interiors and exteriors of buses and trains, as well as stations themselves, are plastered with posters and digital screens promoting everything from new movies to university°.

  • Is there an advertisement that made an impression on you when you were a child?

    Yes. I vividly remember a series of animated commercials for breakfast cereal.

    They featured a catchy Jingle and a colorful cartoon mascot going on adventures, the combination of bright animation music, and the promise of a Free toy inside made it incredibly memorable and effective on my childhood self.

  • What kind of advertising do you like?

    I’m most drawn to minimalist, witty or emotionally intelligent advertising, a clever print AD that uses a play on words, or a short film style AD that tells a genuine story without hard selling a product stands out. I dislike loud, aggressive sales pitches. I prefer ads that respect the audiences, Intelligence and seek to engage rather than just shout at them.

  • Have you ever bought something because of an advertisement?

    Yes, I have last year I bought a facial cleanser because I saw an influencer recommending it on du yan. The idea made it look amazing, but after using it, I found it was just average. Now I’m more careful and read reviews before buying.

Shoes

Questions:

  • Do you like buying shoes? How often?

    I do, but I am a considered shopper rather than an impulsive one.

    I probably add a new pair to my wardrobe, every 8 to 12 months, usually to replace a worn out staple or for a specific purpose, like a new pair of running trainers. I see them as a functional investment rather than a frequent fashion purchase.

  • Have you ever bought shoes online?

    I have. But I approach it with caution. I tend to only buy from brands whose sizing I’m already familiar with, or from retailers with a very clear and Free returns policy.

    The inability to try them on for comfort and fit is a significant drawback.

    So it requires a bit of research and a leap of faith.

  • How much money do you usually spend on shoes?

    It varies dramatically depending on the purpose. I’m happy to spend a significant amount on a high quality, versatile pair of leather boots or professional shoes that will last for years, for casual summer footwear, like sandals.

    I’m much more budget conscious. On average. I’d say I spend a moderate amount prioritizing value over price.

  • Which do you prefer, fashionable shoes or comfortable shoes?

    Comfort wins without question. I firmly believe there’s no need for these to be mutually exclusive.

    As many brands now successfully merge style with ergonomics. However, if forced to choose, I’d always opt for comfort.

    There’s little point in wearing stylish shoes if you’re in too much pain to enjoy yourself or walk confidently.

Names

Questions:

  • Is it easy to remember people’s names?

    Honestly, it’s not very easy for me. I often remember faces, but forget names, especially when I meet several new people at once.

    Their names just slip away. I think names are abstract and don’t stick without repetition.

  • How do you remember people’s names?

    I usually repeat the person’s name immediately after hearing it and try to use it in conversation. I also associate the name with a facial feature or a scene.

    Sometimes I save it in my phone with a small note.

  • How do you feel when people can’t remember your name?

    I would feel a little awkward or disappointed, especially if we’ve met more than once, it might seem like I didn’t leave an impression, but I also understand, because I forget names, too. So I usually just smile and reintroduce myself.

  • Do you often forget people’s names?

    Yes, I often forget people’s names, especially when I meet them for the first time I might remember the face clearly, but the name just disappears. I think it’s because I’m not paying full attention during introductions.

Collecting things

Questions:

  • Do you collect things?

    Yes. I do enjoy collecting things as a hobby. My collection mainly consists of vintage stamps and coins.

    I find joy in exploring the history and cultural significance behind each item.

    Collecting allows me to appreciate the diversity of cultures and the artistry of different time periods.

    It’s a fascinating and educational pastime that brings a sense of fulfillment to my leisure activities.

  • Where do you usually keep things you need?

    I usually keep things I need in an organized manner at home.

    Essential items like keys, wallet, and documents have designated places, making them easily accessible.

    For work related materials, I maintain a well organized work space, utilizing storage solutions and maintaining a clutter Free environment helps ensure that I can quickly locate and retrieve items when needed.

  • Would you keep old things for a long time? Why?

    Yes. I believe in keeping old things for a long time, especially if they hold sentimental value or have historical significance, these items serve as tangible connections to the past, preserving memories and stories, whether it’s family heirlooms, vintage items or meaningful gifts, holding onto them allows me to appreciate the continuity of life and the value of preserving personal and cultural history.

  • Are there any things you have kept from your childhood?

    Yes. I’ve kept a few toys and books from my childhood that hold special memories.

    These items remind me of the carefree days and the joy I experienced while playing and reading.

    They serve as nostalgic keepsakes that I cherish and occasionally look back on to reflect on my past.

Feeling bored

Questions:

  • Do you often feel bored?

    No, I don’t often feel bored, I believe in keeping myself engaged and finding activities that interest me, whether it’s pursuing a hobby, reading or spending time with friends and family.

    I always try to make the most of my time.

    I think there’s so much to explore and learn in the world and staying curious helps me avoid boredom. Additionally, I like to set personal goals, which gives me a sense of purpose and keeps me motivated.

  • Do you think childhood is boring or adulthood is boring?

    I think both childhood and adulthood have their own unique aspects, and whether one finds them boring depends on individual perspectives in childhood.

    There’s often a sense of innocence and wonder with plenty of time for play and exploration. However, as an adult, there’s a different kind of excitement in taking on responsibilities, pursuing personal goals and experiencing a greater sense of independence.

    While childhood memories are filled with carefree moments, adulthood offers a variety of opportunities for personal and professional growth.

  • What do you do when you feel bored?

    When I feel bored, I usually try to make the most of that time by engaging in activities that interest me.

    One of my favorite things to do is to read books, especially those in genres like science fiction or mystery.

    It allows me to escape into different worlds and stimulates my imagination.

    Additionally, I enjoy taking up creative projects, such as writing or experimenting with photography.

    These activities not only keep me occupied, but also provide a sense of accomplishment.

    If the weather is good, I might go for a walk or explore new places as it adds a refreshing element to my routine.

  • When would you feel bored?

    I usually find myself feeling bored when I’m not mentally stimulated, or when I have a lot of Free time with nothing specific to do. For example, during long waits or when there’s a lack of interesting activities, I might start to feel a bit bored.

    However, i’ve learned to combat this by planning my days effectively and filling my Free time with activities that I enjoy, whether it’s reading a book, working on a personal project or engaging in a hobby.

    Staying proactive helps me ward off boredom and make the most of my time.

Computers/tablets

Questions:

  • In what conditions would it be difficult for you to use a computer or tablet?

    The most obvious condition would be in areas with no internet connectivity or power source, rendering them useless.

    It would also be very difficult to use one effectively in a very crowded or bumpy environment, like on a packed train.

  • In what conditions would you use a computer or tablet?

    I primarily use a computer for complex focused work that requires multitasking between several windows.

    I opt for my tablet in more relaxed settings, like when I’m travelling or want to look up a recipe quickly in the kitchen.

  • What would your life be like without computers or tablets?

    It would be profoundly different and considerably more challenging. My productivity at work would plummet, and staying in touch with friends and family abroad would become much more difficult and slower without instant messaging and video calls.

  • When was the first time you used a computer or tablet?

    I first used a desktop computer in primary school around the age of seven or eight.

    It was a very basic model used for simple educational games and learning to type, which felt incredibly advanced at the time.

  • Would you like to use a computer or tablet?

    Definitely. I find a computer indispensable for serious work tasks like writing reports, or analyzing data due to the larger screen and full keyboard.

    A tablet is my go to device for casual browsing, reading, or watching videos on the couch.

Lost and found

Questions:

  • Do you report to the police when finding something lost by others? Why?

    I typically wouldn’t report an item to the police unless it’s something very valuable or important. Like a wallet or a phone.

    For smaller items. I’d prefer to try to find the owner directly or take them to a lost and found.

    Reporting to the police seems more appropriate for significant or sensitive items as it may require official documentation.

  • Have you ever lost things?

    Yes. I have lost things before like my keys or my phone on a few occasions. It can be quite frustrating, especially when I’m in a hurry and can’t find them. However, I try to stay calm and retrace my steps to locate the lost items.

  • What will you do if you find something lost by others?

    If I find something lost by others, I would first try to locate the owner by asking people nearby if they recognize it.

    If I can’t find anyone who claims it, I would take it to a lost and found area if I am in a public place.

    I believe it’s important to help return lost items to their rightful owners whenever possible.

  • Will you post on social media if you lose your item?

    Yes. I might consider posting on social media if I lose something important and cannot find it.

    Sharing a post can quickly reach a wider audience and friends or acquaintances who see it may help me locate the item.

    It’s a practical way to spread the word, especially if I lost it in a public place.

Travelling

Questions:

  • Do you prefer to sit by the window when travelling?

    Yes, I always prefer a window seat.

    When traveling I love watching the scenery pass by, it makes the journey feel more interesting and less boring. If I’m on a plane.

    I also like seeing the clouds and the city below.

  • Did you have a long journey with your family as a child?

    Yes, I remember taking a very long road trip with my family. When I was around aided, we drove from our city to my grandparents’ hometown, which took about 12 hours. I felt tired and carsick.

    But my parents made it fun with snacks and music. It’s a warm memory. Now.

  • Do you often ride a bicycle?

    No, I don’t often ride a bicycle. I used to ride one when I was in school.

    But now I mostly take the subway or bus, the city traffic is quite heavy.

    And I don’t feel safe cycling on the roads. However I sometimes use shared bikes for short trips.

  • What transport do you often use when travelling?

    When traveling, I usually take the train or the plane for long distances, trains are comfortable and I can enjoy the view for shorter trips.

    I take buses or drive in cities, I use the subway or taxis. I choose based on time, cost and convenience.

Street market

Questions:

  • What do people usually buy on the street market?

    People usually buy fresh fruit, vegetables and local snacks at street markets. You can also find cheap household items, clothes, andsometimes handmade crafts, it’s a great place to experience local life and bargain for a good price.

  • Do you prefer to go shopping in the shopping mall or on the street market?

    I generally prefer street markets for daily food because it’s lively and cheap, but for buying clothes, electronics or when the weather is bad.

    I prefer shopping malls. Malls are more comfortable and have better after sales service. So it really depends on what I need.

  • When was the last time you went to a street market?

    The last time I went to a street market was last Saturday morning, I went to the morning market near my home to buy some fruit, and freshly made soy milk for breakfast. The place was crowded and full of energy.

  • Are there many street markets in China?

    Yes, there are many street markets in China. Almost every neighborhood has a morning market, or wet market night markets are also very common, especially in southern cities, they are an important part of daily life and local food culture.

Politeness

Questions:

  • How did you learn to be polite as a child?

    I learned to be polite mainly from my parents. They always reminded me to say, thank you. And please, I also learned from teachers at school watching how polite adults behave around me was probably the biggest influence.

  • Do you think being polite is very important?

    Yes, politeness is extremely important. It shows respect for others and helps create a harmonious environment.

    Polite people are more likely to be trusted and welcomed. Being polite is the most basic social lubricant.

    It costs nothing, but means a lot.

  • On what occasions should we be polite?

    We should be polite on almost all occasions, but especially in formal settings, like meetings, interviews and ceremonies, visiting someone’s home, talking to elders and dealing with customers also require politeness in daily life.

    Simple interactions like ordering food or asking for directions, call for basic courtesy.

  • What did you do to show your politeness as a child?

    As a child, I showed politeness by greeting elders and saying, thank you. I would give my seat to elderly people on the bus at home.

    I waited for adults to start eating before I picked up my chopsticks, I also shared my snacks with visitors.

Tiredness

Questions:

  • Do you often feel tired?

    Yes, I often feel tired, especially after a long day of work or study, sometimes even after waking up.

    I still feel exhausted. I think it’s a combination of physical fatigue and mental stress.

  • When would you feel tired?

    I usually feel tired in the late afternoon. Around 3 or 4 o’clock after lunch.

    My energy drops, and I feel sleepy also after finishing a mentally intense task.

    I feel drained long commutes in the evening, make it worse.

  • What do you do when you feel tired?

    When I feel tired, I usually take a short nap or drink a cup of coffee. Sometimes I go for a quick walk to refresh my mind. If I’m at home, I might listen to some soft music or take a warm shower, the key is to stop and give myself a break.

  • When you feel tired, do you still go out with your friends?

    Yes, usually I still go out with friends even when I’m tired.

    But I might not stay as long. I tell them I’m tired and they understand, sometimes I just sit and listen and their energy actually lifts me up, being together helps me relax.

Rubbish and recycling

Questions:

  • What do you do when you see rubbish on the street?

    I usually pick it up if it’s not too dirty and throw it into a nearby, Benny, if I see someone littering, I might give a polite reminder. I believe keeping streets clean is everyone’s responsibility. Small actions can make a big difference.

  • How do you recycle things like paper and plastic?

    I separate paper, plastic, and glass at home into different bins. Our community has designated recycling stations. I also reuse plastic bags and donate old books to charity. I try to reduce waste first, then recycle what’s left.

  • Is waste sorting common in your country?

    As waste sorting is becoming more and more common in China, many cities now require residents to separate kitchen waste, recyclables, hazardous waste.

    Another way see there are sorting stations in communities and volunteers to Guide people. It’s a national trend, though enforcement varies.

  • Did you recycle when you were a kid?

    Not really when I was a kid, waste sorting wasn’t widely promoted. We only separated recyclable paper and bottles sometimes, because we could sell them for pocket money. Most household waste went into one binning. The awareness came later.

Paper

Questions:

  • Have you made any crafts with paper?

    Yes, I used to make paper planes and origami cranes. When I was a child at school, we would fold paper frogs and raise them on the desk. Last year. I also made a simple paper lantern for a festival. It’s a cheap and fun way to create something.

  • Do you still write physical letters?

    I rarely write physical letters. Now, the last time I wrote one was to my grandmother, because she doesn’t use a smart phone. I think handwritten letters feel more personal and precious.

    But they take too much time, so I usually send messages or emails instead.

  • Do people still keep handwritten letters today?

    Some people do keep them, especially older generations, handwritten letters carry emotional value. They are seen as keepsakes of important times. However, among young people, it is rare. Most letters exist digitally now as screen shots were saved messages.

  • Do you carry paper and pens with you when you go out?

    I usually carry a small notebook and a pen in my bag, but I rarely use them because everything is on my phone. Still.

    I feel safer having them. In case I need to jot down something quickly or my phone dies.

  • What did you like to do with paper as a child?

    As a child, I loved drawing on paper. I would fill every corner with doodles. I also enjoyed folding paper, planes and boats, cutting paper into snowflakes with.

    Is my favorite winter activity. Paper was my first creative toy.

Fruit and vegetables

Questions:

  • How often do you eat fruit and vegetables?

    I eat fruit and vegetables. Every day I try to have at least one apple or banana and vegetables with lunch and dinner. My mother always insisted on this habit, eating them keeps my digestion, good.

    And my skin clear.

  • Where do you usually buy fruit and vegetables?

    I usually buy fruit and vegetables at the local wet market where the supermarket near my home, the wet market has fresher and cheaper produce. Sometimes I order from my grocery APP, if I’m busy.

  • What kind of fruits and vegetables do you dislike?

    I dislike bitter melon, the mosty, its strong bitter taste is hard for me to accept. I also avoid celery because of its stringy texture other than that.

    I enjoy most common vegetables and fruits.

  • Were there any kinds of fruits and vegetables you disliked as a child?

    Yes, as a child, I hated coriander and carrots. My mom had to chop them into tiny pieces and hide them in dumplings. I’ve gradually accepted the Mao, but the childhood aversion was very strong.

  • Do people in your country like planting vegetables?

    Yes, many people in China like planting vegetables, especially the older generation, they grow them on balconies, roofs, or small patches of land. It is partly a habit from rural life and partly for health and saving money. Even some young people are joining this trend.

Secondary school

Questions:

  • Do you remember your first day at secondary school?

    Yes, I remember it very clearly. I was both excited and nervous. The school was much bigger than my primary school. I got lost trying to find my classroom, but my form teacher was kind. And I made a friend on the first day.

  • Were there any subjects that you found difficult at secondary school?

    Yes, mass was quite difficult for me, especially geometry and functions. I often couldn’t understand the logic.

    And the pace of the class was fancy. I had to spend extra time on practice problems just to keep up.

  • What was your favorite subject at secondary school?

    My favorite subject was English. I love learning new words and watching English movies in class. The teacher made lessons fun with games and songs. I felt a sense of achievement.

    When I could express myself in another language.

  • Is there anything you miss about your secondary school?

    Yes, I missed the simple friendship and the carefree days, everyone was so pure and full of dreams. I also missed the canteen food and the little shops near the school gate. Those were the best times of my youth.

Opportunities

Questions:

  • Did you have any opportunities to take part in new activities as a child?

    Yes, I had quite a few opportunities. My parents encouraged me to try different things. I joined a painting class, a swimming club, andeven a small robotics workshop at school trying new activities help me discover what I like. D I’m grateful for those chances.

  • Should people try as many different things as they can?

    I think people should try different things when they are young, but not endlessly trying many activities helps you discover your strengths and interests.

    However, spreading yourself too thin means you never master anything. So it’s about balance, explore broadly first, then focus on what you truly love.

  • Do you like taking on new opportunities?

    Yes, I like taking on new opportunities, they help me grow and learn new things. Even if I fail.

    I gain experiences, new opportunities can be scary at first.

    But they often lead to the best rewards. I try to say, yes, when I can.

  • Do you often get new opportunities?

    No, I don’t often get new opportunities. My life is quite stable and I mostly stick to my routine. However, I do look for opportunities when I want to change something like learning a new skill or meeting new people, they come when I actively seek them.

Morning routines「邪21」

Questions:

  • Do you like to get up early in the morning?

    Yes. I prefer getting up early in the morning as it allows me to kick start my day with a sense of productivity.

    The quietude of the early hours provides me with a peaceful environment to engage in activities like exercise, meditation and planning, setting a positive tone for the day ahead.

  • What do you do right after getting up in the morning?

    Right? After I wake up, I like to take a few moments to stretch and gather my thoughts for the day. Then I brush my teeth and wash my face to feel refreshed. After that, I enjoy a healthy breakfast, usually something like oatmeal or fruit, which gives me energy for the day ahead.

  • Is breakfast important?

    Yes, breakfast is crucial for starting the day, right?

    It provides essential nutrients and energy to kick start metabolism. After a night of fasting.

    Studies show that people who eat breakfast tend to have better concentration mood and overall health compared to those who skip it.

  • What is your morning routine?

    My morning routine begins with waking up at 6:30 am followed by some stretching exercises to invigorate my body. Afterward, I enjoy a nutritious breakfast consisting of oats and fruits. Then I review my schedule for the day and prepare for work or study, ensuring a productive start.

Art「邪21」

Questions:

  • Do you like art?

    Yes. I’m a real enthusiast. I don’t just mean paintings. I appreciate a wide spectrum from sculpture and photography to digital installations.

    I find it’s a powerful medium for expressing complex emotions and ideas that are sometimes hard to articulate with words alone.

  • Do you like visiting art galleries?

    Absolutely. I find it a profoundly enriching experience. It’s not just about viewing the art itself, but also about understanding the historical context and the artists perspective.

    I always leave feeling inspired and with a broader Outlook.

  • Do you want to be an artist?

    While I have immense admiration for artists, I don’t think it’s the right path for me. I lack the technical skill.

    But more importantly, I see myself as more of an appreciator and patron of the arts rather than a creator.

  • Do you like modern art or traditional art?

    I appreciate both for different reasons. Traditional art amazes me with its technical mastery and historical narrative.

    Modern art, however, often challenges my perceptions and invites more personal interpretation.

    I wouldn’t say I prefer one over the other.

Social media「邪21」

Questions:

  • Do you think you spend too much time on social media?

    I believe I spend a reasonable amount of time on social media while it can be easy to get absorbed.

题目为2026年10月21日记录的口语试题，注意时效性

Part 1

Friends

Questions:

  • Do you have a friend you have known for a long time?

    Yes. My closest friend is someone I met on my first day of primary school.

    We’ve maintained our friendship for over two decades, navigating different schools, universities, and cities. That long shared history has created an unbreakable bond and a deep intuitive understanding of each other.

  • Do you often go out with your friends?

    I would say we have a good balance. We make a point to schedule proper outings like trying a new restaurant or going to an exhibition a couple of times a month.

    But we also value simpler, more frequent interactions, like a quick coffee or a phone call, which are just as important for maintaining our connection.

  • Do you prefer to spend time with one friend or with a group of friends?

    I appreciate both dynamics for different reasons.

    One on one time allows for deeper, more intimate and vulnerable conversations.

    Group settings, however, are fantastic for energy, laughter and shared experiences. I don’t have a strong preference.

    It depends entirely on my mood and what I’m seeking from the social interaction.

  • How important are friends to you?

    They are utterly vital. My friends are my chosen family.

    They provide a crucial support system, emotional sustenance, and shared joy. They offer different perspectives, honest advice, and unconditional support through life’s challenges. Making the good times better and the hard times easier to bear.

  • Is there a difference between where you meet friends now and where you used to meet them in the past?

    There’s a significant difference in our teens and early 20s. We almost exclusively met in public places like shopping malls, cinemas, or fast food restaurants.

    Now, as adults, we gravitate much more towards each other’s homes for dinner, or quieter cafes and pubs where we can actually hear each other talk.

  • What do you usually do with your friends?

    Our activities are quite varied. We often go out for meals or coffee to catch up, go for walks in the park or watch films together. Sometimes our meet UPS are even more low key. Just spending an evening, cooking dinner together and talking at home is just as enjoyable.

  • Where do you often meet each other?

    We tend to favor casual, comfortable environments where we can talk without shouting.

    Our most common meeting spots are cozy cafes, each other’s homes or parks when the weather is nice.

    The location is always chosen for its ability to facilitate good conversation.

  • Why are some places suitable for meeting while others are not?

    Suitability hinges on the desired interaction. A noisy sports bar is perfect for watching a match with a group, but terrible for a heart to heart conversation. A library is suitable for studying together, but not for a celebratory party.

    The ideal venue matches the group size and the primary goal of the meeting be it lively socializing or intimate talking.

  • Would you invite friends to your home?

    Absolutely. I consider it the highest form of hospitality and intimacy.

    Inviting someone into your personal space is a sign of trust and comfort.

    Some of my best memories with friends are of informal gatherings at home, cooking together, playing games, and talking for hours without the time constraints of a public venue.

Advertisement

Questions:

  • Do you like advertisements?

    I appreciate well crafted creative advertisements that tell a story or artistically executed. However, I have a strong aversion to intrusive, repetitive, or blatantly manipulative ads. The sheer volume of advertising we are exposed to daily is overwhelming.

    So the ones that earn my attention are those that offer something of value, be it, humour, beauty, or useful Information.

  • Do you often see advertisements when you are on your phone or computer?

    Yes. I frequently encounter advertisements while using my phone or computer. In fact, digital ads are almost unavoidable in China, appearing on social media platforms within apps and as pre roll videos.

    While some can be intrusive, I find many useful, especially those tailored to my interests.

    As they often introduce me to new products or services, I might genuinely like.

  • Do you see a lot of advertising on trains or other transport？

    An enormous amount. Public transport is a prime advertising, real estate, because it captures a captive audience with little else to do during their commute, the interiors and exteriors of buses and trains, as well as stations themselves, are plastered with posters and digital screens promoting everything from new movies to university°.

  • Is there an advertisement that made an impression on you when you were a child?

    Yes. I vividly remember a series of animated commercials for breakfast cereal.

    They featured a catchy Jingle and a colorful cartoon mascot going on adventures, the combination of bright animation music, and the promise of a Free toy inside made it incredibly memorable and effective on my childhood self.

  • What kind of advertising do you like?

    I’m most drawn to minimalist, witty or emotionally intelligent advertising, a clever print AD that uses a play on words, or a short film style AD that tells a genuine story without hard selling a product stands out. I dislike loud, aggressive sales pitches. I prefer ads that respect the audiences, Intelligence and seek to engage rather than just shout at them.

  • Have you ever bought something because of an advertisement?

    Yes, I have last year I bought a facial cleanser because I saw an influencer recommending it on du yan. The idea made it look amazing, but after using it, I found it was just average. Now I’m more careful and read reviews before buying.

Shoes

Questions:

  • Do you like buying shoes? How often?

    I do, but I am a considered shopper rather than an impulsive one.

    I probably add a new pair to my wardrobe, every 8 to 12 months, usually to replace a worn out staple or for a specific purpose, like a new pair of running trainers. I see them as a functional investment rather than a frequent fashion purchase.

  • Have you ever bought shoes online?

    I have. But I approach it with caution. I tend to only buy from brands whose sizing I’m already familiar with, or from retailers with a very clear and Free returns policy.

    The inability to try them on for comfort and fit is a significant drawback.

    So it requires a bit of research and a leap of faith.

  • How much money do you usually spend on shoes?

  • Which do you prefer, fashionable shoes or comfortable shoes?

    Comfort wins without question. I firmly believe there’s no need for these to be mutually exclusive.

    As many brands now successfully merge style with ergonomics. However, if forced to choose, I’d always opt for comfort.

    There’s little point in wearing stylish shoes if you’re in too much pain to enjoy yourself or walk confidently.

Names

Questions:

  • Is it easy to remember people’s names?

    Honestly, it’s not very easy for me. I often remember faces, but forget names, especially when I meet several new people at once.

    Their names just slip away. I think names are abstract and don’t stick without repetition.

  • How do you remember people’s names?

    I usually repeat the person’s name immediately after hearing it and try to use it in conversation. I also associate the name with a facial feature or a scene.

    Sometimes I save it in my phone with a small note.

  • How do you feel when people can’t remember your name?

    I would feel a little awkward or disappointed, especially if we’ve met more than once, it might seem like I didn’t leave an impression, but I also understand, because I forget names, too. So I usually just smile and reintroduce myself.

  • Do you often forget people’s names?

    Yes, I often forget people’s names, especially when I meet them for the first time I might remember the face clearly, but the name just disappears. I think it’s because I’m not paying full attention during introductions.

Collecting things

Questions:

  • Do you collect things?

    Yes. I do enjoy collecting things as a hobby. My collection mainly consists of vintage stamps and coins.

    I find joy in exploring the history and cultural significance behind each item.

    Collecting allows me to appreciate the diversity of cultures and the artistry of different time periods.

    It’s a fascinating and educational pastime that brings a sense of fulfillment to my leisure activities.

  • Where do you usually keep things you need?

    I usually keep things I need in an organized manner at home.

    Essential items like keys, wallet, and documents have designated places, making them easily accessible.

    For work related materials, I maintain a well organized work space, utilizing storage solutions and maintaining a clutter Free environment helps ensure that I can quickly locate and retrieve items when needed.

  • Would you keep old things for a long time? Why?

    Yes. I believe in keeping old things for a long time, especially if they hold sentimental value or have historical significance, these items serve as tangible connections to the past, preserving memories and stories, whether it’s family heirlooms, vintage items or meaningful gifts, holding onto them allows me to appreciate the continuity of life and the value of preserving personal and cultural history.

  • Are there any things you have kept from your childhood?

    Yes. I’ve kept a few toys and books from my childhood that hold special memories.

    These items remind me of the carefree days and the joy I experienced while playing and reading.

    They serve as nostalgic keepsakes that I cherish and occasionally look back on to reflect on my past.

Feeling bored

Questions:

  • Do you often feel bored?

    No, I don’t often feel bored, I believe in keeping myself engaged and finding activities that interest me, whether it’s pursuing a hobby, reading or spending time with friends and family.

    I always try to make the most of my time.

    I think there’s so much to explore and learn in the world and staying curious helps me avoid boredom. Additionally, I like to set personal goals, which gives me a sense of purpose and keeps me motivated.

  • Do you think childhood is boring or adulthood is boring?

    I think both childhood and adulthood have their own unique aspects, and whether one finds them boring depends on individual perspectives in childhood.

    There’s often a sense of innocence and wonder with plenty of time for play and exploration. However, as an adult, there’s a different kind of excitement in taking on responsibilities, pursuing personal goals and experiencing a greater sense of independence.

    While childhood memories are filled with carefree moments, adulthood offers a variety of opportunities for personal and professional growth.

  • What do you do when you feel bored?

    When I feel bored, I usually try to make the most of that time by engaging in activities that interest me.

    One of my favorite things to do is to read books, especially those in genres like science fiction or mystery.

    It allows me to escape into different worlds and stimulates my imagination.

    Additionally, I enjoy taking up creative projects, such as writing or experimenting with photography.

    These activities not only keep me occupied, but also provide a sense of accomplishment.

    If the weather is good, I might go for a walk or explore new places as it adds a refreshing element to my routine.

  • When would you feel bored?

    I usually find myself feeling bored when I’m not mentally stimulated, or when I have a lot of Free time with nothing specific to do. For example, during long waits or when there’s a lack of interesting activities, I might start to feel a bit bored.

    However, i’ve learned to combat this by planning my days effectively and filling my Free time with activities that I enjoy, whether it’s reading a book, working on a personal project or engaging in a hobby.

    Staying proactive helps me ward off boredom and make the most of my time.

Computers/tablets

Questions:

  • In what conditions would it be difficult for you to use a computer or tablet?

    The most obvious condition would be in areas with no internet connectivity or power source, rendering them useless.

    It would also be very difficult to use one effectively in a very crowded or bumpy environment, like on a packed train.

  • In what conditions would you use a computer or tablet?

    I primarily use a computer for complex focused work that requires multitasking between several windows.

    I opt for my tablet in more relaxed settings, like when I’m travelling or want to look up a recipe quickly in the kitchen.

  • What would your life be like without computers or tablets?

    It would be profoundly different and considerably more challenging. My productivity at work would plummet, and staying in touch with friends and family abroad would become much more difficult and slower without instant messaging and video calls.

  • When was the first time you used a computer or tablet?

    I first used a desktop computer in primary school around the age of seven or eight.

    It was a very basic model used for simple educational games and learning to type, which felt incredibly advanced at the time.

  • Would you like to use a computer or tablet?

    Definitely. I find a computer indispensable for serious work tasks like writing reports, or analyzing data due to the larger screen and full keyboard.

    A tablet is my go to device for casual browsing, reading, or watching videos on the couch.

Lost and found

Questions:

  • Do you report to the police when finding something lost by others? Why?

    I typically wouldn’t report an item to the police unless it’s something very valuable or important. Like a wallet or a phone.

    For smaller items. I’d prefer to try to find the owner directly or take them to a lost and found.

    Reporting to the police seems more appropriate for significant or sensitive items as it may require official documentation.

  • Have you ever lost things?

    Yes. I have lost things before like my keys or my phone on a few occasions. It can be quite frustrating, especially when I’m in a hurry and can’t find them. However, I try to stay calm and retrace my steps to locate the lost items.

  • What will you do if you find something lost by others?

    If I find something lost by others, I would first try to locate the owner by asking people nearby if they recognize it.

    If I can’t find anyone who claims it, I would take it to a lost and found area if I am in a public place.

    I believe it’s important to help return lost items to their rightful owners whenever possible.

  • Will you post on social media if you lose your item?

    Yes. I might consider posting on social media if I lose something important and cannot find it.

    Sharing a post can quickly reach a wider audience and friends or acquaintances who see it may help me locate the item.

    It’s a practical way to spread the word, especially if I lost it in a public place.

Travelling

Questions:

  • Do you prefer to sit by the window when travelling?

    But my parents made it fun with snacks and music. It’s a warm memory. Now.

  • Do you often ride a bicycle?

    No, I don’t often ride a bicycle. I used to ride one when I was in school.

    But now I mostly take the subway or bus, the city traffic is quite heavy.

    And I don’t feel safe cycling on the roads. However I sometimes use shared bikes for short trips.

  • What transport do you often use when travelling?

    When traveling, I usually take the train or the plane for long distances, trains are comfortable and I can enjoy the view for shorter trips.

    I take buses or drive in cities, I use the subway or taxis. I choose based on time, cost and convenience.

Street market

Questions:

  • What do people usually buy on the street market?

    The last time I went to a street market was last Saturday morning, I went to the morning market near my home to buy some fruit, and freshly made soy milk for breakfast. The place was crowded and full of energy.

  • Are there many street markets in China?

    Yes, there are many street markets in China. Almost every neighborhood has a morning market, or wet market night markets are also very common, especially in southern cities, they are an important part of daily life and local food culture.

Politeness

Questions:

  • How did you learn to be polite as a child?

    Yes, politeness is extremely important. It shows respect for others and helps create a harmonious environment.

    Polite people are more likely to be trusted and welcomed. Being polite is the most basic social lubricant.

  • On what occasions should we be polite?

  • What did you do to show your politeness as a child?

    As a child, I showed politeness by greeting elders and saying, thank you. I would give my seat to elderly people on the bus at home.

Tiredness

Questions:

  • Do you often feel tired?

    I feel drained long commutes in the evening, make it worse.

  • When you feel tired, do you still go out with your friends?

    Yes, usually I still go out with friends even when I’m tired.

Rubbish and recycling

Questions:

  • What do you do when you see rubbish on the street?

  • How do you recycle things like paper and plastic?

    I separate paper, plastic, and glass at home into different bins. Our community has designated recycling stations. I also reuse plastic bags and donate old books to charity. I try to reduce waste first, then recycle what’s left.

  • Is waste sorting common in your country?

    As waste sorting is becoming more and more common in China, many cities now require residents to separate kitchen waste, recyclables, hazardous waste.

Paper

  • Have you made any crafts with paper?

    But they take too much time, so I usually send messages or emails instead.

  • Do people still keep handwritten letters today?

    Some people do keep them, especially older generations, handwritten letters carry emotional value. They are seen as keepsakes of important times. However, among young people, it is rare. Most letters exist digitally now as screen shots were saved messages.

  • Do you carry paper and pens with you when you go out?

    I usually carry a small notebook and a pen in my bag, but I rarely use them because everything is on my phone. Still.

    I feel safer having them. In case I need to jot down something quickly or my phone dies.

  • What did you like to do with paper as a child?

    As a child, I loved drawing on paper. I would fill every corner with doodles. I also enjoyed folding paper, planes and boats, cutting paper into snowflakes with.

    Is my favorite winter activity. Paper was my first creative toy.

Fruit and vegetables

Questions:

  • How often do you eat fruit and vegetables?

    I eat fruit and vegetables. Every day I try to have at least one apple or banana and vegetables with lunch and dinner. My mother always insisted on this habit, eating them keeps my digestion, good.

    And my skin clear.

  • Where do you usually buy fruit and vegetables?

    I usually buy fruit and vegetables at the local wet market where the supermarket near my home, the wet market has fresher and cheaper produce. Sometimes I order from my grocery APP, if I’m busy.

  • What kind of fruits and vegetables do you dislike?

    I dislike bitter melon, the mosty, its strong bitter taste is hard for me to accept. I also avoid celery because of its stringy texture other than that.

    I enjoy most common vegetables and fruits.

  • Were there any kinds of fruits and vegetables you disliked as a child?

    Yes, as a child, I hated coriander and carrots. My mom had to chop them into tiny pieces and hide them in dumplings. I’ve gradually accepted the Mao, but the childhood aversion was very strong.

  • Do people in your country like planting vegetables?

    Yes, many people in China like planting vegetables, especially the older generation, they grow them on balconies, roofs, or small patches of land. It is partly a habit from rural life and partly for health and saving money. Even some young people are joining this trend.

Secondary school

Questions:

  • Do you remember your first day at secondary school?

    Yes, I remember it very clearly. I was both excited and nervous. The school was much bigger than my primary school. I got lost trying to find my classroom, but my form teacher was kind. And I made a friend on the first day.

  • Were there any subjects that you found difficult at secondary school?

    Yes, mass was quite difficult for me, especially geometry and functions. I often couldn’t understand the logic.

    And the pace of the class was fancy. I had to spend extra time on practice problems just to keep up.

  • What was your favorite subject at secondary school?

    My favorite subject was English. I love learning new words and watching English movies in class. The teacher made lessons fun with games and songs. I felt a sense of achievement.

    When I could express myself in another language.

  • Is there anything you miss about your secondary school?

    Yes, I missed the simple friendship and the carefree days, everyone was so pure and full of dreams. I also missed the canteen food and the little shops near the school gate. Those were the best times of my youth.

Opportunities

Questions:

  • Did you have any opportunities to take part in new activities as a child?

  • Should people try as many different things as they can?

    However, spreading yourself too thin means you never master anything. So it’s about balance, explore broadly first, then focus on what you truly love.

  • Do you like taking on new opportunities?

    I gain experiences, new opportunities can be scary at first.

    But they often lead to the best rewards. I try to say, yes, when I can.

  • Do you often get new opportunities?

    No, I don’t often get new opportunities. My life is quite stable and I mostly stick to my routine. However, I do look for opportunities when I want to change something like learning a new skill or meeting new people, they come when I actively seek them.

Morning routines「邪21」

Questions:

  • Do you like to get up early in the morning?

    The quietude of the early hours provides me with a peaceful environment to engage in activities like exercise, meditation and planning, setting a positive tone for the day ahead.

  • What do you do right after getting up in the morning?

    Right? After I wake up, I like to take a few moments to stretch and gather my thoughts for the day. Then I brush my teeth and wash my face to feel refreshed. After that, I enjoy a healthy breakfast, usually something like oatmeal or fruit, which gives me energy for the day ahead.

  • When do most children begin to have their own opinions?

    Children usually start forming their own opinions around age four or five at this age.

    They begin to say no and ask why by primary school, they can express clear preferences for food, clothes and activities. In teenage years, they develop stronger and more independent views on life.

  • Do children communicate more with teachers or with parents?

    Younger children tend to communicate more with parents because they depend on them. However, teenagers often share more with teachers or friends. They may feel parents don’t understand them. Also they spend a lot of time at school.

    So teachers become important mentors in their daily lives.

  • Whose opinions are more important to children, their parents’ or teachers’?

    It really depends on the child’s age for young children. Parents’ opinions are usually the most important, because they provide a sense of security. But as children grow older, especially in their teenage years, teachers and friends opinions often start to matter more. They spend more time at school and want to gain approval from people outside the family.

  • Who do most young people like to share opinions with?

    I think most young people prefer to share their opinions with close friends rather than family members or teachers. The main reason is that people of a similar age usually have shared in interests, similar experiences and comparable ways of thinking.

    So it’s easier for them to understand each other.

    Also, many young people are worried about being judged, were criticized by older generations, especially when talking about sensitive topics like relationships, career choices or personal values. Friends often provide emotional support instead of giving lectures, which makes conversations feel more relaxed and comfortable. At the same time, social media has also become an important place for young people to express their opinions, public directly and interact with others online.

近期改变

Questions:

  • Do you think it is good to change one’s daily routine?

    I think changing your daily routine occasionally is very healthy. A fixed routine can become boring and kill creativity by making small changes.

    Like taking a different route to work or trying a new hobby, you stimulate your brain and stay more engaged.

    It also helps you adapt to unexpected situations better. So a little variety keeps life fresh and exciting.

  • Do you think it is good to change jobs?

    Changing jobs can be very beneficial if done for the right reasons it can lead to higher pay new skills and a fresh environment, staying in one position to long sometimes limits growth.

    However, switching too often makes you look unreliable. So it’s good. When you have learned all you can and need a new Challenge to keep growing.

  • Is it good for people to get a job promotion?

    Getting a promotion is generally positive. It usually means more money and recognition, which boosts motivation and self esteem. However, promotions often come with much higher pressure and longer hours. If someone is not ready.

    It can lead to burnout. So it’s good only when the person truly wants the new responsibilities.

  • Do people often make plans around their regular routines?

    Yes, people often do routines, provide a natural structure.

    So they plan errands and social events around work and meal times. For example.

    People schedule meetings during office hours and gym sessions after work, even leisure activities like watching shows are planned for evenings, plans revolve around what’s already fixed in their daily schedule.

  • Who tend to change their daily routine more, young people or old people?

    Young people definitely change their routines. More often, their lives are less settled with new jobs, relationships, and social activities constantly shifting. They are also more open to trying new things, older people value stability, and their bodies are used to a fixed rhythm change for them can feel disruptive rather than exciting.

当地新闻

Questions:

  • Do people read the newspaper where you live?

    Physical newspapers are rarely read now, especially among young people most get news from apps like Taobao or work at.

    Feeds. However, some older people still keep the habit of reading a paper copy in the morning, but overall digital news has almost completely replaced traditional newspapers where I live.

  • Do people prefer local or international news?

    It depends on the person. Most ordinary people care more about local news because it directly affects their daily life.

    Like transport and policies. However, younger and more educated people follow international news closely, too, especially about technology and global events, local news feels practical.

    While international news provides a broader world view.

  • Do you think it’s important to have a national identity?

    Yes, I think having a national identity is important, it gives people a sense of belonging and shared history in a globalized world.

    It helps preserve unique cultures and traditions. It also unites citizens during crises like natural disasters. However, it should not turn into extreme nationalism that rejects everything foreign.

  • How can people develop their national identity?

    People can develop national identity by learning history and understanding the sacrifices made by past generations.

    Participating in traditional festivals and cultural activities also deepens the connection traveling within the country and appreciating its diverse landscape helps too.

    Most importantly, contributing to the community through small daily acts makes you feel truly part of the nation.

遇到困难终成功的人

Questions:

  • In your country, what industry is it easier to be successful in?

    In China, I think the technology and internet industry offers the most opportunities for success. Right now, the market is huge.

    And there is strong government support, e commerce, short videos, and AI are booming. However, competition is extremely fierce. So you still need innovation and hard work.

  • What’s the difference between ordinary people and successful people?

    Ordinary people often do what is required.

    While successful people go the extra mile, successful people are also more willing to take risks and learn from failure. They tend to have a clearer vision and stronger self discipline. Most importantly, they don’t wait for opportunities, they create them.

  • What are the factors leading to people’s success?

    Many factors lead to success, hard work and persistence are the foundation, because without them, talent is wasted, good timing and luck.

    Also play a part like being in the right industry at the right time, strong social connections and family support often open doors. However, the most crucial factor is the ability to learn and adapt quickly.
